name: Luseogliflozin

overview.mechanism: Reduces renal tubular glucose reabsorption, increasing urinary glucose excretion.
uses: Glucose-lowering treatment studied in adults with type 2 diabetes; confirm the locally approved indication and prescribing information.

paragraphs.text: A single-dose study in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes included eGFR groups from normal kidney function to severe impairment (15–29 mL/min/1.73 m²). Urinary glucose excretion increased in every group, but the increase was smaller at lower eGFR. This pharmacodynamic result should not be treated as evidence of equivalent glucose-lowering efficacy across CKD stages.
This was a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study, not a kidney-outcome trial. Its inclusion of severe impairment does not by itself supply an approved chronic dose or dialysis schedule.

evidence.title: Dedicated renal trial: primary endpoint not met

paragraphs.text: The RESOLUTION randomized, open-label trial enrolled 152 patients with type 2 diabetes and eGFR based on serum creatinine of 15–45 mL/min/1.73 m². Change in eGFR at 104 weeks, the primary endpoint, did not differ significantly between luseogliflozin and control.

An early eGFR decline occurred after starting luseogliflozin. The subsequent chronic eGFR slope was numerically less negative but not significantly different overall. Favorable subgroup findings were exploratory and do not override the nonsignificant primary result or establish prevention of kidney failure.
